results.scenario: Broke a leg in a road accident; policy is 10 days old.
results.rationale: Initial 30-day waiting period does not apply to accidental hospitalisation.
results.summary: The broken leg from a road accident is covered because inpatient hospitalisation is included and the accident exemption removes the initial waiting period.

results.rationale: Cataract needs 24 months of continuous cover.
results.summary: Cataract surgery is covered in principle, but the 24‑month specific‑illness waiting period is not satisfied because the policy is only 18 months old.
rejectionRisks: Specific‑illness waiting period not met (policy age 18 months < 24 months required)

results.scenario: Chose a deluxe room costing above 1% of the sum insured.
results.rationale: Room rent capped at 1% of SI/day; higher category => proportionate payment.
results.summary: Room charges are covered but a waiting‑period check is missing, so the claim outcome cannot be determined fully.
rejectionRisks: Waiting period may not be satisfied if policy is less than 30 days old (initial waiting period).
Room‑rent cap limits reimbursement to 1% of Sum Insured per day; deluxe room cost above this will be reduced proportionately.

results.rationale: Maternity expenses need 24 months of continuous cover.
results.summary: Maternity expenses are covered only after a 24‑month waiting period, but the policy is only 12 months old.
rejectionRisks: Maternity waiting period not satisfied (policy age 12 months < 24‑month requirement)

results.rationale: Post-hospitalisation covered only up to 60 days after discharge.
results.summary: Medicines purchased 75 days after discharge exceed the 60‑day post‑hospitalisation limit, so the claim is not payable.
rejectionRisks: Expense incurred beyond the post‑hospitalisation time window (75 days > 60 days)
